CORRECTION, earlier pass: the ORIGINAL segment A (ticks 0-18, contiguous)
sampled DS:0x282, DS:0x17a/0x17c, DS:0x377 and DS:0xa/0xc at an unpinned

value of the tick that just ran (hero/state) and the ENTERING value of the
NEXT tick (camera -- continuous, so leaving-T equals entering-T+1),
building one honest tick=T record pairs the camera field from the
cursor=T read with the hero/state fields from the cursor=T+1 read.

This shape -- long stretches of genuine lockstep, growth concentrated in

[STATIC]: tools/replay-diff.mjs constructs `new Arsenal(weapons)` and
never once calls `.equip()` on it -- every one of the three weapon slots
keeps `weapon = -1` (Slot's own constructor default) for the WHOLE
replay. `allocateShots` (src/game/weapons.js) returns null for any slot
with `weapon < 0`, so `Arsenal#allocate()` always returns null and
`Player#_tryFire()` always returns false, UNCONDITIONALLY, for every
tick of this harness's own replay. The original, by contrast, genuinely
carries a weapon here -- CS:0x8FD2 grants one of THREE fixed loadouts
(2x5+6x3, or 2x3/5x5/4x1 -- see checks.js's own "the attract-mode grant
is NOT a starting loadout" note) keyed on the same DS:0x3e6 attract-
cycler state joyg1's own spawn table uses; WHICH of the three applies to
joyg1 specifically is NOT established by this pass -- so a future fix
here needs that resolved first, it is not simply "add one equip() call".
Whichever it is, a fire press while walking genuinely enters the
fire-halt states (5 right / 6 left, CS:0x5D46-family, which this port's
own player.js documents as moving nothing for their whole animation
cycle) in the original, while this harness's hero just keeps walking
through every single fire press, because it structurally cannot ever
succeed at firing.
[PROVEN, from data already in this file]: every state=5 sample already
